 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  This is the time set aside for members of the public to address the City Council on
  items of interest that are not on the Agenda, but are within the subject matter
  jurisdiction of the San Gabriel City Council. Pursuant to the Brown Act, the City
  Council cannot answer any questions or take any action until such time as the
  matter may appear as an item on a future agenda.

  In an effort to provide everyone with an opportunity to speak tonight, please be
  aware that all public comments will be limited to a maximum of three minutes. You
  will receive a 30-second warning as you approach the end of your time. As a
  reminder, please be respectful of all speakers regardless of the position they take
  on any items.

  If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a speaker’s request card
  and hand it to the clerk before the start of the meeting. When speaking, please
  state your NAME for the record.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 19-31 TO UPDATE THE CITY’S CITYWIDE
  FEE SCHEDULE

  The Citywide Fee Schedule represents the fees charged by the City for various
  licenses, permits, facility rentals, and services provided to residents, developers,
  program users and the general public. In accordance with the Fiscal
  Sustainability Policy and past practice, the schedule is reviewed, revised, and
  presented to the City Council for consideration annually.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-31 adopting the
  recommended fees set forth within the City’s Citywide Fee Schedule to become
  effective immediately upon passage.

  B. INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING OF AN ORDINANCE AMENDING
  TITLE XI, SECTION 110 OF THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE- BUSINESS
  LICENSES

  Adoption of the referenced Ordinance amending Title XI, Section 110 of the
  San Gabriel Municipal Code will add a provision for exempting certain
  performers at City-sponsored events and any Community Services recreation
  program individual instructors, coaches and/or referees from business license
  fees, add a provision for prorating business license fees for non-San Gabriel
  vendors at City-sponsored events, and correct various business license fees to

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 17, 2019  3
   match the amount adopted within Ordinance 356 –C.S. on July 16, 1991. No
  business license taxes are being added or increased.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Waive full reading, read by title only, and introduce for first reading
  Ordinance No. 654 amending Title XI, Section 110 of the San Gabriel
  Municipal Code, pertaining to Business License Taxes; and

  2. Direct the City Clerk to schedule the second reading and adoption of
  Ordinance No. 654 for the next regular City Council Meeting.

  C. ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT TO UPDATE THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL
  CODE RELATING TO ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS (ZTA19-001)

  On June 19, 2018, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 644 regarding the
  development of Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) with a vote of 5-0. Over the
  past year, Planning Division staff has seen a number of inquiries come in from
  the public regarding ADUs. This “clean up” Zone Text Amendment (ZTA) would
  delete references to previous accessory unit options, provide clarification to
  ADU development, and add a requirement for a covenant to be recorded with
  all future ADU applications.

  On August 12, 2019, the Planning Commission, which serves as the
  recommending body, considered the proposed ZTA and recommended that
  City Council adopt Ordinance No. 653. The City Council considered this item at
  a public hearing on September 3, 2019. At the public hearing, the City Council
  discussed the proposed ZTA, requested additional information, and continued
  the item to the September 17, 2019 Regular City Council Meeting.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Conduct the public hearing and discuss the proposed Ordinance;

  2. Motion to waive full reading and introduce the attached Ordinance by title
  only. The City Clerk will read aloud the full title of the Ordinance.

 6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT ISSUES

  Over the past few years, cities in the San Gabriel Valley have been experiencing
  an increase in the number of human-coyote incidents and encounters. Several
  cities in the San Gabriel Valley adopted individual wildlife management plans
  to reduce human-coyote conflicts within their communities. Additionally, there
  is a need for municipalities and elected officials in the San Gabriel Valley to
  collectively coordinate coyote management efforts. The San Gabriel Valley
  Council of Governments (SGVCOG) formed a task force and, as a result, is now
  introducing the Regional Coyote Management Framework (RCMF) that cities
  may consider to participate in for a cost of $20,000 for the next two years.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council consider the several options provided
  for in the staff report and provide direction for staff to proceed.

  Should the City Council approve the MOA, authorize $10,000 to be transferred
  from the General Fund contingency account to pay for the implementation of
  the agreement.

  B. CONSIDERATION OF CREATING A CITY TOWING SERVICE FRANCHISE
  AGREEMENT

  California State Legislation gives law enforcement agencies the ability to seize
  and impound vehicles for 30 days whose drivers are either unlicensed or are
  driving while their driver’s license is suspended or revoked. Rather than the
  industry standard franchise agreement, the City of San Gabriel currently
  operates its police-imitated tow service through an informal agreement. While
  the informal agreement with Dickson’s Tow has been satisfactory, the benefits
  of a towing service franchise agreement include a reduction in City liability and

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 17, 2019  5
   exposure, better control of the service provided to the public, and a method of
  cost recovery for City administrative costs. These agreements ensure
  appropriate authorities and responsibilities are identified for the security of
  vehicles and other property in addition to administration of police-related
  vehicle impounds, storage, and other tow-related operations. Overall, a
  franchise agreement would ultimately ensure the quality and professionalism
  of the towing service representing the City.

  Recommended Action:

  It is recommended that the City Council direct staff to proceed with the drafting
  of a Tow Service Franchise Ordinance and the preparation and release of a
  Request for Qualifications for tow service providers.

  C. URGENCY ORDINANCE AMENDING TITLE III, SECTION 34 OF THE SAN
  GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE PURCHASING PROCEDURES

  The purchasing section of the Municipal Code was last updated in 2008 with
  the adoption of Ordinance No. 576-C.S. which updated §34.32 Informal
  Contract Procedures. The City Council also updated its Purchasing Policy on
  August 17, 2010, by minute order. In reviewing the two documents, it became
  apparent that an update to the Municipal Code was necessary to match
  provisions in the Purchasing Policy and current purchasing practices. Adoption
  of the referenced Urgency Ordinance amending Title III, Section 34 of the San
  Gabriel Municipal Code will update the purchasing procedures section to
  modify and clarify purchasing policies and procedures used to procure goods
  and services for City operations.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt as an Urgency Ordinance,
  Ordinance No. 656 amending Title III, Section 34 of the San Gabriel Municipal
  Code, pertaining to Purchasing Procedures.

  D. 2019 SAN GABRIEL DUMPLING AND BEER FEST

  As part of the Fiscal Year 2019-2020 Budget, the City Council allocated funding
  of community engagement events and programs. Staff is requesting to use a
  portion of those funds for the 5th Annual San Gabriel Dumpling and Beer Fest
  on Friday, October 4, 2019, from 6:00 p.m. to 10:30 p.m. in the historic Mission
  District. The City is the host and producer of the event and plans to work with
  KCM Agency again this year to help coordinate the award-winning event for
  the community. Staff recommends that the City Council approve the agreement

   with KCM Agency and authorize an expenditure of $21, 400 from the
  community engagement account (#121-714-00-27-047) for the production of
  the 2019 San Gabriel Dumpling and Beer Fest.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the Professional Services Agreement with KCM Agency; and

  2. Authorize, if necessary, an expenditure not to exceed $21, 400 from the
  community engagement account #121-714-00-27-047 for the production
  of the 2019 San Gabriel Dumpling & Beer Fest.
